answer.evidence: Rows 4-8 form a 5-row grey band that brightens toward the front. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a standing cabinet prop with two glowing arched glass doors, so it matches the prop references. Its 13 visible tones per tile sit between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted: a dark blue-grey frame edge and brown-dark lines around the yellow panels, not a sticker-style black line. The yellow panels show a ramp from light yellow through yellow and orange to a brown shadow, with mullions and a lower detail row. The frame has about 3-4 value steps, a thin lighter rim and a darker inner edge. It reads a little smoother and less grainy than the stall and well, which have per-tile highlights and speckle, so density is slightly lower. Still, there are no flat fills and the shading is clearly more than a flat body with an outline, so a careful artist would accept it next to the references.
